Subject: E2E delay acceptance checklist & next steps (post-call)

Samir / Aisha — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick post-call recap and proposed acceptance checklist so we can line up a short validation run before you decide on migration timing. I focused the checklist on the end-to-end latency requirements you raised (p95 / p99) plus streaming/concurrency behavior.

Recap of goals from the call:
- Target deck: p95 end-to-end (client->server->client) under production traffic shape: 125–150 ms target; p99 no worse than 450 ms for the primary 512-token inference profile.
- Steady-state throughput target: 100–120 RPS sustained with spikes to 300 RPS for short bursts.
- Streaming behavior: support 8 concurrent streaming flows per user session; total concurrent open streams ~600 across the cluster.
- Failure modes: graceful fallback to smaller model variant with <30% added latency when capacity stalls.

Proposed acceptance checklist (what Redwood will deliver for validation):
1) Baseline run: 30-minute steady-state at 120 RPS with your production traffic mix (we'll use the CSV you shared). Collect p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end and server-only.
2) Spike run: 10-minute burst to 300 RPS to validate tail behavior and autoscaling reaction.
3) Streaming concurrency test: synthetic clients to maintain 600 concurrent open streams and verify per-stream token latency under 8 concurrent writers.
4) Cold start/scale test: simulate a rolling restart to observe cold KV-cache warmup impact on p99.
5) Instrumentation and logs: capture per-request IDs, per-hop timing, and KV-cache hit ratios. We'll provide an OpenTelemetry shim to inject trace IDs.
6) Acceptance thresholds: p95 <= 150 ms, p99 <= 450 ms (end-to-end) OR documented regression mode with a fallback plan.

Data and artifacts we'll need from you to run the above:
- initial-traffic-profile.csv (sampled tokens, seq lengths, streaming vs non-streaming split) — you attached a version on the call; please confirm final file.
- example API keys and an allowlist IP range (for short POC duration).
- a short list (3) of production-critical routes you want prioritized for routing/pinning during the run.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Redwood will provide a test harness + run plan within 24 hours of finalizing the traffic CSV.
- We propose a 48–72 hour window for the validation runs to allow a steady-state plus replay/retune.
- Post-run: we will share a results pack (raw traces, aggregate latency histograms, autoscaler logs) and a short recommendations doc with configuration changes if we miss thresholds.

Attachments referenced: call-recording.mp4, initial-traffic-profile.csv, slo-targets.xlsx

Next steps / asks:
- Can you confirm the traffic CSV and the 3 routes you want in-scope by EOD Wednesday (May 26)?
- Can your infra team provide a short-lived allowlist for Redwood test agents?

Thanks — I can schedule the runs as soon as we have those.

Best,
Alex Martinez

Alex — thanks for this summary and the clear checklist. A few clarifications from our side before we lock in dates:

1) The traffic CSV attached in this reply is the canonical one ("initial-traffic-profile-v2.csv"). It includes a larger streaming percentage than we showed on the call (about 42% streaming).
2) Our current provider's reported numbers (attached) show p95 ~ 220 ms and p99 ~ 920 ms end-to-end under our 100 RPS steady-state. We want to be conservative in expectations; hitting your p95 target would be a strong win but we need a clear path if p99 remains elevated.
3) For the in-scope routes: /api/v1/chat (high concurrency, streaming), /api/v1/generate (batch-oriented), /api/v1/summary (short sequences).
4) We can provide an allowlist from our infra for the POC window; please send the IPs your agents will use.

Requested from Redwood before we start:
- A small example load script (wrk or k6) and the OpenTelemetry shim so our infra can do a quick internal check.
- Can you run one short pilot on our side with only 30 RPS so we can validate instrumentation ingestion first?

Attaching: current-provider-tail-latency.csv (snap from last week), initial-traffic-profile-v2.csv
